sources.name: CBN Approved Guidelines for Bureau de Change Operations in Nigeria (May 2024)
CBN: Economics of Digital Currencies, A Book of Readings
CBN Circular BPS/PSV/DIR/GEN/CIR/01/001: Statements of Payment Finality for the Nigerian Payments Schemes
Legal 500: Summary of the Revised Licence Categorisation for Operators in the Nigerian Payments System

entries.subject: payment_finality_rtgs
entries.value_text: when the sending bank's account is debited and the receiving bank's account is credited
entries.display: RTGS payments are final and irrevocable once the sending bank is debited and the receiving bank credited
entries.quote: At the point when the sending bank’s account is debited and the receiving bank's account is credited, paymient/settlement is final and cannot be revoked
entries.notes: Circular date line OCRs as 'JULY 1074, 2017'; the year 2017 is reliable, the day is not. Quoted text keeps the OCR typo 'paymient'.

entries.subject: payment_finality_card
entries.value_text: when the issuer authorises the transaction
entries.display: Card payments are final and irrevocable at the moment the issuer authorises the transaction
entries.quote: Payment is considered final and irrevocable when the issuer AUTHORISES the transaction. At this point, the transaction cannot be unwound and settlement MUST occur.

entries.subject: payment_finality_instant_payment
entries.value_text: when the IP switch sends the authorisation response to the presenting bank
entries.display: Instant payments are final and irrevocable when the instant payment switch sends the authorisation response to the presenting bank
entries.quote: At the point when IP Switch sends authorisation

entries.subject: payment_finality_mobile
entries.value_text: when the switch successfully transmits the authorisation message from the sending MMO to the beneficiary MMO
entries.display: Mobile money payments are final when the switch transmits the authorisation message from sending MMO to beneficiary MMO
entries.quote: This is at the point when the switch successfully transmits the authorization message from the sending MMO to the beneficiary MMO

entries.subject: bdc_tier1_minimum_capital
entries.display: Tier 1 BDC licence: minimum capital N2,000,000,000
entries.notes: Table row OCR'd on one line: Tier 1 = N2,000 million, Tier 2 = N500 million, per the '(N' million)' column header.

entries.subject: bdc_tier2_minimum_capital
entries.display: Tier 2 BDC licence: minimum capital N500,000,000
entries.notes: Second column of the same table row: Tier 2 minimum capital N500 million.

entries.subject: bdc_cryptocurrency_dealing
entries.display: A BDC may not deal in cryptocurrency or with entities dealing in crypto assets
entries.quote: Dealing in cryptocurrency or with entities dealing in cryptocurrency, crypto assets or such other virtual assets.

entries.subject: bdc_international_outward_transfer
entries.display: A BDC may not carry out international outward transfers
entries.notes: Listed under 'Non-Permissible Activities'; short quote is the whole item as printed.

entries.subject: bdc_deposit_taking
entries.display: A BDC may not take deposits from or grant loans to the public in any currency
entries.quote: Taking deposits from or granting loans to members of the public in any currency and in any form.

entries.subject: customer_funds_holder
entries.display: Only mobile money operators may hold customer funds; PSSPs and other payment licensees may not
entries.quote: The Circular prescribes that only MMOs are permitted to hold customer funds.
entries.notes: Secondary summary of the CBN revised licence categorisation circular; existing licensees had to comply by 30 June 2021.

entries.subject: mmo_minimum_capital
entries.display: Mobile Money Operator licence: minimum capital N2,000,000,000
entries.quote: In addition to the old permissible activities for MMOs, MMOs can now also carry out Super-Agent activities. Minimum Capital – N2,000,000,000.00
entries.notes: Table row for licence category 1 (Mobile Money Operation).

entries.subject: enaira_status
entries.value_text: Africa's first central bank digital currency
entries.display: The eNaira is the first central bank digital currency in Africa
entries.quote: the Retail projects in the Index are led by the Central Bank of Nigeria's (CBN) eNaira, the first CBDC in Africa
entries.notes: CBN publication; effective_from is the year of publication, exact day not printed on the cited page.

notes: Payment finality is stated per scheme rather than as a single rule. BDC prohibitions are quoted from the non-permissible activities list.
